pr_title: fix(chromium): wait for request extra info before firing Page.Response
pr_comments: Closing as the added complexity doesn't seem justified. Will wait for more feedback and revisit this if there is enough demand.

issue_context.title: [BUG] request.headers() is flaky in Chromium
issue_context.body:
Looks like `Network.requestWillBeSentExtraInfo` sometimes comes too late and `response.request().headers()` returns incomplete headers.
```
  1) page/page-network-request.spec.ts:84:4 › [chromium] should get the same headers as the server =

    Error: expect(received).toEqual(expected) // deep equality

    - Expected  - 9
    + Received  + 0

      Object {
    -   "accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/avif,image/webp,image/apng,*/*;q=0.8,application/signed-exchange;v=b3;q=0.9",
    -   "accept-encoding": "gzip, deflate, br",
    -   "cache-control": "max-age=0",
    -   "connection": "keep-alive",
    -   "host": "localhost:8907",
    -   "sec-fetch-dest": "document",
    -   "sec-fetch-mode": "navigate",
    -   "sec-fetch-site": "none",
    -   "sec-fetch-user": "?1",
        "upgrade-insecure-requests": "1",
        "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) HeadlessChrome/92.0.4500.0 Safari/537.36",
      }

      93 |     const response = await page.goto(server.PREFIX + '/empty.html');
      94 |     // console.log(serverRequest.headers);
    > 95 |     expect(response.request().headers()).toEqual(serverRequest.headers);
         |                                          ^
      96 |     console.log(i + ' - done');
      97 |   }
      98 | });

        at /home/yurys/playwright/tests/page/page-network-request.spec.ts:95:42
        at WorkerRunner._runTestWithBeforeHooks (/home/yurys/playwright/node_modules/folio/out/workerRunner.js:275:13)
```

We also experienced this flake in Python.
Yeah, in java it fails almost every run on the bots.
Given extra implementation complexity we decided to wait for customer reports of the problem and revisit it later if need be.

#### Why was this issue closed?

We are prioritizing the bugs based on the upvotes, recency and our ability to act. It looks like this issue only has a handful of upvotes, has not been touched recently and/or we lack sufficient feedback to act on it. We are closing issues like this one to keep our bug database maintainable. Please feel free to open a new issue and link this one to it if you think this is a mistake.
